candidates.name: Käthe Kollwitz Museum
candidates.content: Käthe Kollwitz's reputation as a social activist who used art as a means to express her support of pacifism was hard-won. Her son was killed in the World War I, after which her art took a turn for the morose. When her grandson was

candidates.name: Hamburger Bahnhof – Museum für Gegenwart
candidates.price: €10, concession €5, under 18 years free. Free entry for everyone every first Thursday of the month from 16:00-20:00
candidates.content: Museum of Contemporary Art located in former Hamburger Bahnhof train station. Big halls filled with artworks made since 1960s. In 2004 Rieckhallen, former Lehrter Bahnhof, was opened and now provides exhibition space for the Fried

candidates.name: Stasi Museum
candidates.content: This museum describes the procedures applied by the East German secret police. Every Friday to Monday, there is a guided tour in English at 15:00 (5€).

candidates.name: Museum Karlshorst
candidates.content: In this house the surrender of Germany was signed on May 9th, 1945, ending WWII in Europe. This museum describes the history of the war between Germany and the Soviet Union between 1941 and 1945 and the GDR/German-Russian relation

candidates.name: Topography of Terror
candidates.content: This outdoor and indoor history museum documents the terror applied by the Nazi regime. It is on the site of buildings which during the Nazi regime from 1933 to 1945 were the headquarters of the Gestapo and the SS, the principal i

candidates.name: Jewish Museum Berlin
candidates.price: Adults €6, concessions €3. Reduced admission if you show a ticket from the nearby Berlinische Galerie
candidates.content: Designed by Daniel Libeskind with an excellent exposition on the Jewish life in Berlin and the impact of the Holocaust. You can easily spend a day here. There is a metal scanner and other security features you'd rather expect at a

candidates.name: German Museum of Technology
candidates.content: Huge technical museum, on a former railroad depot, featuring from ancient water and wind mills to computer pioneer Konrad Zuse's inventions, a collection of old to new vehicles of all types -bicycles, boats, trains, etc - and the

candidates.name: East Side Gallery
candidates.content: The longest stretch of the Berlin Wall still in existence, painted by artists in 1991 and restored in 2009, after years of decay. At Mühlenstraße, next to the river Spree. The murals are painted on the east side of the wall after

candidates.name: Computerspielemuseum
candidates.content: Exhibition of digital interactive entertainment culture. You can actually play almost all of the exhibits making it a more "hands on" museum than most.

candidates.name: Museum in der Kulturbrauerei
candidates.content: Find out how it felt to live in East Germany in this modern and well-presented exhibition. The museum is a good starting point if you only have a few minutes to sneak a quick peek inside an East German family's living room, but yo

candidates.name: Museum for Architectural Drawing
candidates.content: The museum is in an iconic building opened in June 2013, showcases privately owned collection of architectural drawings from the twentieth and twenty-first centuries..

candidates.name: Deutsches Historisches Museum
candidates.content: German historical museum covering everything from pre-history up to the present day. One can spend many, many hours here! The building from 1695/1730 was the Zeughaus (Arsenal) until 1876.

candidates.name: Friedrichswerdersche Kirche
candidates.content: Nice church near Unter den Linden/Museum Island, finished in 1830 by Schinkel in English Neogothic style. Nice exhibition inside (neoclassical statues and an exhibition about Schinkel's life and work upstairs).

candidates.name: Tränenpalast
candidates.content: Millions of visitors leaving East Berlin by train said tearful goodbyes to their friends and relatives from the East at this former border checkpoint. Hardly a year after the wall came down, the building was turned into a nightclu

candidates.name: Französischer Dom
candidates.content: The French cathedral houses the Hugenottenmuseum. It represents the ongoing influence on Berlin by the Huguenots who emigrated from France after the revocation of the Edict of Nantes. Crown Prince Friedrich William encouraged them

candidates.name: Pergamon Museum
candidates.price: Admission: €19, discounted: €9.50, children under age of 18 free
candidates.content: There are three huge collections housed within this grand building: the Collection of Classical Antiquities, the Museum of Near Eastern Antiquities and the Museum of Islamic Art. The Pergamon Museum was the last museum built on Mu

candidates.name: Altes Museum
candidates.price: Admission: €10, discounted: €5, children under age of 18 free
candidates.content: The main floor houses the antiquities collection in an ongoing exhibit called "Neue Antike im Alten Museum" (New Antiquities in the Old Museum). Directly through the front door, entering from the Lustgarten (Pleasure Garden, now u

candidates.name: Alte Nationalgalerie
candidates.price: Admission: €10, discounted: €5, children under age of 18 free
candidates.content: Specializes in 19th-century painting and sculpture; Monet, Manet, Cézanne, C. David Friedrich and other important 18th- and 19th-century artists are well-represented.

candidates.name: Bode-Museum
candidates.price: Admission: €10, discounted: €5, children under age of 18 free
candidates.content: The museum’s treasures include the sculpture collection with works of art from the middle ages to the 18th century. The Bode museum is best known for its Byzantine art collection and the coin cabinet.

candidates.name: Nikolaikirche
candidates.content: Berlin's oldest church (1230) is a 3-nave hall church. It is in the centre of an area destroyed by bombs in the war which was then turned into a faux "old town" by the East German authorities called Nikolaiviertel. The area is mor

candidates.name: Hanfmuseum
candidates.content: It is the only hemp museum in Germany; you can see the history of hemp, the culture and use of it. You can see hemp grow. There is a cafe downstairs, with an open WiFi access. Everything going on here is legal - including the hemp

candidates.name: DDR Museum
candidates.content: A museum dedicated to everyday life in communist East Germany. The museum has very relaxed rules and you are allowed to touch and examine almost every object, which adds greatly to the experience.

candidates.name: Reichstagsgebäude
candidates.content: This imposing building houses the Federal German Parliament or "Bundestag" and was completed in 1894 to meet the need of the newly-unified German Empire of the Kaisers for a larger parliamentary building. The Reichstag was intende

candidates.name: Bauhaus-Archiv / Museum für Gestaltung
candidates.content: Closed for renovations; the temporary Bauhaus-Archiv is at Knesebeckstraße 1-2 in Charlottenburg. Building designed by Walter Gropius. Inside a museum, library, cafe and shop.

candidates.name: Ramones Museum Berlin
candidates.alt: Temporarily closed, check website for updates
candidates.content: Pays tribute to the Punk band The Ramones. It displays more than 300 unique and original Ramones memorabilia. You can get a drink at cafe Mania inside the museum. DeeDee Ramone grew up in Berlin and the city is mentioned in severa

candidates.name: Gemäldegalerie
candidates.content: The Gemäldegalerie contains an astounding array of paintings, including works by Rembrandt, Rubens, Botticelli, Raphael, Titian, Goya, Velasquez and Watteau. The collection contains works from the old Bodemuseum on Museumsinsel in

candidates.name: Museum für Naturkunde
candidates.content: More than 30 million objects in the scientific collection and a fascinating exhibition in one of the most significant institutions of its kind in the world. Some parts still under construction.

candidates.name: Spandau Citadel
candidates.content: A fortress built between 1560 and 1590 to Italian design on the site of a 12th-century castle. The Juliusturm housed part of the huge indemnity (in physical gold coins) France had to pay after the war of 1870/71 until what was lef

candidates.name: Berlinale – Berlin Film Festival
candidates.content: The city's largest cultural event and an important fixture in the global film industry's calendar (up there with Cannes). 250,000 tickets sold, 400 different films screened and a host of associated parties and events every year. I

candidates.name: Young Euro Classic
candidates.content: A music festival established in 2000 that features youth orchestras from around the world. The concerts take place in the Konzerthaus Berlin on Gendarmenmarkt. The festival usually runs for around 2 weeks. Concerts often feature w

candidates.name: Festival of Lights
candidates.content: A 10-day-long festival when famous buildings in Berlin are illuminated in a special way.

candidates.name: Fuckparade
candidates.content: It was founded in 1997 as a counter-movement to the commercialized Love Parade, and has evolved into an annual political demonstration for the preservation of Berlin's underground club culture and against gentrification. Unlike ma

candidates.name: Artemis
candidates.content: When the unpredictable weather in Berlin isn't favourable to explore the city's cultural gems, Artemis makes up for it with its wellness facilities. Aimed at relaxation, no children or electronic devices are allowed to make a full

candidates.name: Kienberg
candidates.content: Before or after visiting the "Gardens of the World", tourists might be interested in climbing on top of the Kienberg (a small hill nearby with a view on the surrounding suburbs) or to go for a walk in the valley of the Wuhle (a sm

candidates.name: IGA Cable Car
candidates.price: Return ticket €6.50 (it is not part of the BVG fare system)
candidates.content: A cable car built for the international gardening exhibition in 2017 which remained in operation afterwards.

candidates.name: Uber Arena
candidates.alt: known as "Mercedes Benz Arena" from 2015-2024, and "O2 world" before then
candidates.content: A modern indoor sports and concert venue, it is among other things the permanent home of Alba Berlin, Berlin's premier Basketball team and Eisbären Berlin, the professional Ice Hockey club of Berlin.

candidates.name: Mauerpark
candidates.content: At the end of the Eberswalder Straße, it was once a piece of the Berlin wall. Today in the summer it is a nice place to be, especially for young people. There's an interesting flea market going on every weekend. In the summer week

candidates.name: KulturBrauerei
candidates.content: A complex that was once a brewery. There you can find the Jazz Cafe, the SODA restaurant where you can enjoy a fine meal of insects, and some clubs: Club 23, nbi and frannz. The KulturBrauerei also has several cinemas showing alte

candidates.name: Friedrich Ludwig Jahn Sportpark
candidates.content: A soccer and American Football stadium with track and field facilities which has been host to several important competitions in the past, including German Bowls (finals of the German American Football League) from 2012 to 2018.

candidates.name: Maxim Gorki Theater
candidates.content: The smallest municipal theatre in Berlin. It was an important venue for contemporary theatre in the German Democratic Republic (GDR). Nowadays its program continues with its political critique. Next to productions of classics, it

candidates.name: Friedrichstadt-Palast
candidates.content: Berlin's biggest show with over 100 artists on the biggest theater stage in the world.

candidates.name: Komische Oper Berlin
candidates.content: Founded in 1947 and at the forefront of modern opera. Their orchestra also performs regular concerts. Guided tours behind the scenes are offered. Each seat has subtitles where you can choose your language.

candidates.name: Staatsoper Unter den Linden
candidates.content: The impressive building and royal history make the building alone worth a visit. The building reopened in December 2017 after extensive refurbishments and acoustic improvements. The general music director of the Staatsoper and its

candidates.name: Berliner Philharmonie
candidates.content: The Berliner Philharmonie is a concert hall with 2,440 seats in Berlin-Tiergarten (constructed from 1960 to 1963 and designed by Hans Scharoun) and the home of the Berlin Philharmonic Orchestra. It is a famous building with outsta

candidates.name: Kindl-Bühne Wuhlheide
candidates.content: The Kindl-Bühne Wuhlheide is a cultural heritage site and of Berlin's largest and most popular open-air stages for rock, pop and electronic concerts in the shape of an ancient amphitheater.

candidates.name: Fähre F24
candidates.hours: May-October 11:00-19:00, crosses the river as often as needed
candidates.content: Make a crossing with the only human-powered ferry run by Berlin's public transport company BVG. The F24 is operated with a rowing boat, and you can use your valid BVG ticket or buy a ticket on site. It needs 12 strokes of an oar t

candidates.name: Strandbad Müggelsee
candidates.content: The history of this heritage-protected public bathing beach at Müggelsee traces back to the 1910s. It has a more than 500 meters long beach and a capacity for 25,000 guests.

candidates.name: Berlin Tour by public bus line 100 and 200
candidates.content: The 100 and 200 bus lines are just ordinary bus lines, but they pass by many of Berlin's famous landmarks. Both run every 5–10 minutes between S+U-station Zoologischer Garten and S+U-station Alexanderplatz. All BVG tickets are acc

candidates.name: Clärchens Ballhaus
candidates.price: Entrance fee depending on event: usually free on weeknights, €5 on weekends
candidates.hours: Daily from 11:00 usually to 00:00 on weeknights, and around 04:00 on weekends); hot food 12:00-22:30, garden closes 23:00, dance starts 21:00
candidates.content: Traditional dance hall and restaurant established 1913. One of the few surviving Berlin ballrooms from the pre-WW1 era, featuring a hall of mirrors. Primarily known for its dance events (be it Disco, Swing, Salsa, Tango, Cha-Cha o

candidates.name: Sisyphos
candidates.content: This techno club is located in a former factory for dog biscuits in Berlin's Rummelsburg neighborhood. It has two indoor dance floors and a large open-air area.

candidates.name: About Blank
candidates.content: This techno club founded by a leftist collective is in a rundown industrial area. The club is known for its endless niches and corners and has two floors and a garden. Guests should know which DJs are playing this night.

candidates.name: Berghain/Panorama Bar
candidates.content: Techno club in an old cogeneration plant near the Ostbahnhof. It has a huge dancefloor and room for more than 1500 people. Panorama Bar upstairs is open late until Sunday afternoon. Gay friendly, with hidden darkrooms and leatherb

candidates.name: Club der Visionäre
candidates.content: Atmospheric club at the waterside well-known for minimal techno, house and techno-house and high-grade DJ bookings. Originally only a summer venue, it now also has an indoor winter location at the MS Hoppetosse excursion ship whic

candidates.name: Lokschuppen Berlin
candidates.content: Techno club with an indoor dancefloor in a former railway depot, an outdoor dancefloor and a garden. It is 100 meters away from the Warschauer Straße S-Bahn station on the former RAW railway compound. Techno, electro and house boo

candidates.name: Matrix
candidates.content: This long-standing dance music club is located within ten claybrick vaults beneath the Warschauer Straße U-Bahn station. Once purely electronic, it nowadays offers a wide range of dance music genres. With its sociable atmosphere i

candidates.name: YAAM
candidates.content: Large reggae/dancehall, hip-hop and afrobeat club in the factory building which previously housed the clubs Maria am Ostbahnhof and Deli an der Schillingbrücke. A focus on street art and street sports and a beach bar in summer.

candidates.name: Pfefferberg
candidates.content: This is a large former brewery compound which has been reused as a cultural and nightlife center with changing clubs, bars, theaters, restaurants, a large beer garden, a hostel and artist's studios for decades. It is a bit similar

candidates.name: Kumpelnest 3000
candidates.content: This tiny dive bar was founded in 1987 by an arts student and originally a venue where gay-lesbian, punk and postpunk guest mingled. While located in an otherwise emptied residential area with no further nightlife, alone the visua

candidates.name: Weekend Club
candidates.content: The Weekend is a rooftop club on the historic Haus des Reisens high-rise building with a view over the Alexanderplatz and the Fernsehturm. The rooftop garden is on the 17th floor. The music played is hip hop, R'n'B, Afrobeats and

candidates.name: KitKatClub
candidates.content: The clubbing concept of the KitKatClub is mixing techno/electro/trance music with fetish parties. Nonstop party from Saturday night to Sunday evening. Be careful and open-minded, and respect the strict dresscode of fetish, latex,

candidates.name: Tresor
candidates.content: The history of this club dates back to 1990s and the start of techno/house scene in Berlin. The old venue in the vault space of the former Wertheim department store in Leipziger Strasse was closed in 2005, but Tresor reopened in M

candidates.name: Arena Club
candidates.content: This techno club in a raw and run-down old boiler room of 500 m² provides the perfect atmosphere for hard industrial techno. It has one dance floor and two bars and an impressive light installation at the ceiling. Next to the club

candidates.name: Zur letzten Instanz
candidates.content: Often claimed to be Berlin's oldest restaurant. While there has been an establishment at the site since 1621, the current name dates back to 1924. What's more is that much of the original building was damaged in World War II and r

candidates.name: Genazvale
candidates.price: appetizers: €4-23, salads: €12-22, breads: €12-23; dumplings: €3-4; soups: €9-11; vegetables: €9-18; mains: €17-27
candidates.content: Delicious Georgian restaurant with pretty decor including Georgian rugs, some of them depicting ancient Georgian churches, and old photographs of people in traditional Georgian garb, and a sound track of pleasant Georgian music.

candidates.name: Mustafas Gemüse Kebap
candidates.price: Chicken döner with vegetable: €2.90, vegetable kebap: €3.50
candidates.content: Regarded as the best Döner Kebab in Berlin. Mustafas is a local institution and draws crowds of tourists and Berliners day and night. Expect to stand in line for 20-40 minutes to get your kebab, which attests to the reputation tha

candidates.name: Sarod's Thai Restaurant
candidates.content: This authentic Thai restaurant offers great food made from fresh ingredients. The ambiente and staff are nice and friendly, and they know English (and Thai, for that matter). Most meals are available as a small portion.

candidates.name: Angus Restaurant Steak-Haus
candidates.content: Pizza, pasta, different steaks etc. It's one of the cheapest restaurants in Kreuzberg and because of this very crowded (which is part of the nice atmosphere).

candidates.name: Burgeramt
candidates.price: €7.50 for a basic burger, €4.50 for fries.
candidates.content: Huge selection of gourmet burgers at reasonable prices. Mediterranean, gorgonzola/walnut, vegetarian, etc., with plenty of homemade relishes and dressings. There is a take-away shop in no 22 and a restaurant in no 21, but the benc

candidates.name: Nil Sudanesische Spezialitäten
candidates.content: Unique place with ethnic cuisine from Sudan. Wonderful place for anybody who would like to taste something from Africa, like quark cheese with fenugreek and black cumin or peanut soup - different and original.

candidates.name: FrischeParadies Bistro
candidates.content: Small bistro inside upscale supermarket. Sit at the small tables or at the bar, where you can watch the chef prepare your meal from scratch with fresh high quality ingredients. The food is simple and fresh, always excellent cuts o

candidates.name: Kopps
candidates.content: Vegan restaurant with upmarket touch that specialises in rather typical German dishes like Roulade or Cordon Bleu that Vegans would normally not eat. Weekend brunch from 09:30 - 16:00.

candidates.name: Tiergartenquelle
candidates.content: Real German dishes, properly prepared and big. Also some local beers available.

candidates.name: Kantina von Hugo
candidates.content: Small cozy Mediterranean mama-style home cooking situated near the Landwehrkanal. The menu is small but changes everyday. Friendly and not too expensive, very nice wines. Fresh pasta is a must.

candidates.name: Lisboa Bar am Boxi
candidates.content: Portuguese tapas, bread, wine, beer and coffee. Good place to have a real dinner or just hang our and share a bottle of wine with a couple of tapas

candidates.name: Neukölln Arkaden
candidates.content: An abundance of clothing stores and eateries, a post office, gym, a cinema known as "Karli" (movies in both German and Turkish shown regularly), and a very large supermarket (Kaufland) in the basement. Free wi-fi.

candidates.name: Markthalle Neun
candidates.content: A market hall.

candidates.name: Öz-Gida
candidates.content: There are Turkish supermarkets all over town, but this one is particularly big and has great items. If you want to have a picnic lunch, consider buying some small containers from their spreads counter, as they are really delicious

candidates.name: Karstadt Hermannplatz
candidates.content: Built in 1929; large shopping center including clothing, book, and beauty products shops, a post office, and its own high-end supermarket, (probably only second to KaDeWe in the area). The grocery section of Karstadt has fresh mea

candidates.name: boxoffberlin
candidates.content: Only 100 m from Checkpoint Charlie you will find a small but very interesting place for extraordinary souvenirs and gifts made by local designers. The gallery shows changing exhibitions of contemporary art, films and more from Ber

december.text: Detailed maps can be found in every U-Bahn station and on the trains. U-Bahn stations can be seen from far by their big, friendly blue U signs. Szczecin (Stettin; 150 km) — The train line is closed for construction until December 2025, but the bus is cheap and faster.

Historischer Weichnatsmarkt Friedrichshain: An atmospheric Christmas market with a charming medieval theme.
Zyankali Bar: The most adventurous bar in Berlin. You'll be surprised what kind of drinks they have on their beverage list. They say some people entered the Zyankali and never came out again.
